name: Sulphide Glacier

waypoints.name: Shannon Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Baker Lake Road (Forest Road 11) north from SR 20 near milepost 82, then turn onto FR 1152 and follow the 1152-014 spur to its end at about 2,500 feet, where the trail begins. The spur is rough and rutted, so high clearance is the sensible minimum for the drive in. If you're staying overnight in the park, you'll need a North Cascades backcountry permit, obtained in person at Marblemount or arranged with the wilderness office ahead of time.

waypoints.name: Timberline Junction
waypoints.directions: Follow Shannon Ridge Trail #742, an old roadbed heading northeast, for about 2 miles to where the road tread ends near 3,800 ft, weaving through a belt of blowdown. Continue on true trail angling left through brush onto the open ridge crest and up to timberline near 4,600 ft, where snow often lingers into midsummer.

beta: From the campsites (6,245 ft for lower camps), head north up the west side of the Sulphide Glacier up rolling steps. At approximately 7,600 feet, terrain flattens and route continues northeast toward summit pyramid. The finish climbs the 3rd-4th class central gully up the south face of the summit pyramid.
